chunks: 72 - Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-'Ubaydi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Abi Hashim al-Bazzaz, from Hanan, from Mu'awiyah, from Tarif ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: Inform me about a man who sold his wife. He said: “The man's hand is to be cut off, and the woman is to be stoned. As for the one who bought her, if he had intercourse with her, then if he was muhsan he is to be stoned, if he knew; and if he was not muhsan he is to be flogged one hundred lashes. And the woman is to be stoned if the one who bought her had intercourse with her.”
73-73 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-'Abbas ibn Musa al-Baghdadi, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Sinan ibn Tarif, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, and he mentioned something of the same meaning, with its wording advanced and delayed.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report includes, namely that his hand is to be cut off, is not required on the basis that he was a thief, because theft only applies to that which may validly be owned, when it is stolen from a specific place and reaches a specific amount, as we shall explain later. A free woman cannot validly be owned in any manner, so when ownership is invalid, cutting off the hand is not required for the one who sold her on the basis that he was a thief. It is possible that this only became obligatory for him on the basis that he was one who spreads فساد in the earth; and whoever is such, the Imam has the choice regarding him between cutting off his hand and foot, or crucifying him, or banishing him from the land, in accordance with what Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in His saying:
“The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land...” — the verse.

key_terms.السَّرِقَةَ: theft, discussed here in order to deny that the punishment is on that basis
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ مُخَيَّرٌ: the Imam has discretionary choice among specified punishments
key_terms.الْحُرَّةُ: a free woman, who cannot validly be owned
key_terms.تُرْجَمُ: she is to be stoned as the hadd punishment mentioned here
key_terms.تُقْطَعَ يَدُهُ: his hand is to be cut off as a prescribed punishment in this report
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through prior valid marriage, carrying the hadd of stoning in zina when conditions are met
key_terms.مُفْسِدًا فِي الْأَرْضِ: one who spreads corruption in the land
key_terms.يُجْلَدَ مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ: he is to be flogged one hundred lashes if not muhsan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shi'i hadith on a man who sells his wife and on the one who has intercourse with her after buying her?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling concerning a man who purported to sell his wife and the punishments connected to the resulting illicit act. The compiler then clarifies that the cutting of the hand is not due to theft, since a free woman cannot be owned, and suggests that the punishment may instead fall under the category of spreading corruption in the land.
